correctness.rationale: For every odd prime p>=5, at scale p−1 in C_(2p) only opposite pairs are nonedges, hence the clique complex is the p-dimensional cross-polytope boundary S^(p−1). Rotation is signed cyclic coordinate shift with characteristic polynomial λ^p+1, a (-1)-axis plus m=(p−1)/2 primitive complex weights 1,3,...,p−2. The equator E=S^(p−2) has free C_(2p) action; the hemisphere construction yields the actual geometric orbit X=cone(E/C_p) attached to E/C_(2p) via the twofold lens covering. Van Kampen gives π1=C2; the universal double covering S^(p−1)/C_p=Σ(E/C_p) has π2≅H2≅H1(E/C_p)=C_p. Lens-space cellular homology and orientation-preserving double covering, with transfer injectivity on p-torsion, give H_odd=C2 in degrees 1,...,p−2 and zero other positive integral homology. This equals RP^(p−1) homology but π2 differs. Independent exact checks enumerated 3^5−1=242 and 3^7−1=2186 nonempty faces and the cycle-distance predicate; the proof, not finite examples, gives the all-prime statement.
residual_risks: Independent checks covered only p=5,7 as finite corroboration and examined the actual verifier script for p=5,7,11; no finite homology table by itself proves the infinite family.
